nodes.name: Every 30 Minutes
nodes.notes: Queue-driven: a missed run just means the next one finds more due (Section 7). Every 30 minutes, not every 6 hours: the host is often up for only a few hours, and n8n's schedule trigger skips an N-hour tick whose clock hour is less than N hours after the last run's clock hour -- it compares hours of the day, not elapsed time. On 2026-10-02 that skipped the only tick in 9 days that found follow-ups due. A 30-minute interval never enters that check (build guard below).

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: follow_up_days=6 and max_follow_ups=2 are parsed out of Section 9 at build time. now_override must stay empty (dry-run only).

parameters.query:
-- Find Due Follow-Ups -- Section 9: "if no reply after N days, generate
-- follow-up draft back into the review queue. Maximum M follow-ups, then mark
-- lost." Queue-driven like every stage (Section 7): whatever is due, whenever
-- this runs.
--
-- $1 now_override ('' in the shipped workflow), $2 days, $3 maximum, $4 batch.
--
-- The clock restarts at the later of the last send and the last follow-up
-- drafted, so a follow-up the reviewer rejected does not spawn the next one the
-- same afternoon. A rejected follow-up still uses its slot: the reviewer
-- decided against it, and writing another would ask again.
--
-- A RETIRED follow-up is not one. Its variant is prefixed 'retired/' (the 41
-- unsent AI-composed follow-ups, 2026-10-19), so it matches neither
-- 'follow-up-%' below nor Write Follow-Up's dedupe: it uses no slot and
-- restarts no clock, and the lead gets the template follow-up of that number.
--
-- Since 2026-10-19 the follow-up is a fixed template (Section 9, Workflow 6),
-- so each due row carries what the template and the gate need and nothing
-- else: the first email as sent and its subject (it is quoted, and "Re:"
-- threads on it), the company name and the contact (the greeting), and the
-- gate's inputs -- the address, whether it is verified, the country (its Send
-- clock), the blocklist flags and settings.auto_approve_email. No claims
-- library: a template follow-up says only the approved wording. CROs only: the
-- template speaks to a CRO, so a site or SMO is never due.
WITH clk AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif($1, '')::timestamptz, now()) AS now
),
sends AS (
  SELECT o.lead_id, o.sent_at, o.message_body, o.draft_id
    FROM outreach_log o
   WHERE o.channel = 'email' AND o.message_id IS NOT NULL
),
first_touch AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.lead_id) s.lead_id, s.sent_at, s.message_body, d.subject
    FROM sends s
    JOIN drafts d ON d.id = s.draft_id
   WHERE coalesce(d.variant, '') NOT LIKE 'follow-up-%'
   ORDER BY s.lead_id, s.sent_at
),
last_send AS (
  SELECT lead_id, max(sent_at) AS sent_at FROM sends GROUP BY lead_id
),
-- created counts follow-up NUMBERS, not rows: a #1 the operator rejected and
-- had regenerated (2026-10-03, leads 7, 91, 104) is still one slot, the way
-- Write Follow-Up's dedupe already reads it. Counted as rows, the second #1
-- took #2's slot and the lead was marked lost instead of followed up again.
fu AS (
  SELECT d.lead_id,
         count(DISTINCT regexp_replace(d.variant, '[/+].*$', ''))::int  AS created,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.status IN ('pending', 'approved'))::int AS open,
         max(d.created_at)                                              AS last_created
    FROM drafts d
   WHERE d.channel = 'email' AND d.variant LIKE 'follow-up-%'
   GROUP BY d.lead_id
)
SELECT l.id                                                             AS lead_id,
       CASE WHEN coalesce(fu.created, 0) >= $3::int THEN 'mark-lost' ELSE 'draft-follow-up' END AS action,
       coalesce(fu.created, 0) + 1                                      AS next_follow_up,
       ft.subject                                                       AS first_subject,
       ft.message_body                                                  AS first_body,
       to_char((ft.sent_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')                                                    AS first_sent_at,
       to_char((ls.sent_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')                                                     AS last_sent_at,
       l.country                                                        AS country,
       l.domain                                                         AS domain,
       -- CRO, site or SMO: lead_company_type(), the one definition (migration 019).
       lead_company_type(e.raw_extraction, l.source)          AS company_type,
       auto_approve_email_enabled()                                     AS auto_approve_email,
       l.company_name                                                   AS company_name,
       c.name                                                           AS contact_name,
       c.email                                                          AS email,
       coalesce(c.verified, false)                                      AS verified,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blocklist b WHERE lower(l.domain) = b.domain OR lower(l.domain) LIKE '%.' || b.domain)                                                 AS lead_domain_blocked,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blocklist b WHERE lower(split_part(c.email, '@', 2)) = b.domain OR lower(split_part(c.email, '@', 2)) LIKE '%.' || b.domain)                                                 AS recipient_domain_blocked
  FROM leads l
  JOIN first_touch ft ON ft.lead_id = l.id
  JOIN last_send ls   ON ls.lead_id = l.id
  LEFT JOIN enrichments e ON e.lead_id = l.id
  LEFT JOIN contacts c ON c.lead_id = l.id
  LEFT JOIN fu        ON fu.lead_id = l.id
  CROSS JOIN clk
 WHERE l.status = 'sent'
   AND lead_company_type(e.raw_extraction, l.source) = 'CRO'
   AND greatest(ls.sent_at, coalesce(fu.last_created, ls.sent_at)) <= clk.now - make_interval(days => $2::int)
   AND coalesce(fu.open, 0) = 0
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM outreach_log o WHERE o.lead_id = l.id AND (o.replied OR o.outcome = 'bounced'))
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inbound_messages i
                    WHERE i.lead_id = l.id AND i.classification IN ('reply', 'opt-out', 'bounce'))
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blocklist b WHERE lower(l.domain) = b.domain OR lower(l.domain) LIKE '%.' || b.domain)
 ORDER BY l.id
 LIMIT $4::int;

nodes.name: Find Due Follow-Ups
nodes.notes: CRO leads at 'sent', no reply, no bounce, not blocklisted, quiet for 6 days: the next follow-up, or 'lost' once 2 have been used.

nodes.name: Build Follow-Up
nodes.notes: The fixed follow-up templates (Section 9, Workflow 6, LOCKED wording, approved 2026-10-19), written by drafting's own template functions (code_template.js above its 'Node body' marker, embedded verbatim): the greeting rules, the cleaned company name, #1 closing with the lead's arm's close (lead_id even A, odd B), Re: the first subject and the first email quoted. No model call. Then the same gate as a first touch: approved unless there is no verified deliverable address, no Send clock or a blocklisted domain. A mark-lost row carries no draft.

parameters.query:
-- Write Follow-Up: insert the follow-up draft, or mark the lead lost. Both
-- guarded so a repeated run is a no-op: a lead gets each follow-up NUMBER at
-- most once, and only a lead still at 'sent' moves. A template follow-up's
-- variant is 'follow-up-1/template/A' (+ hold tags); a composed one from
-- 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-19 carries claim codes ('follow-up-1/BEN-DECK.A1'), and
-- one from before that is the bare 'follow-up-1' -- so the number is compared,
-- not the variant.
--
-- The draft is 'pending' -- the reviewer's queue, with hold_reason -- unless
-- the gate approved it: only a payload marked approved_by 'auto' comes out
-- approved, and the table's trigger (migration 020) re-checks that against the
-- live flag, the template variant, the address and the blocklist.
WITH p AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS p
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO drafts (lead_id, channel, variant, subject, body, status, approved_by, hold_reason)
  SELECT (p.p->>'lead_id')::bigint, 'email', p.p->'draft'->>'variant', p.p->'draft'->>'subject',
         p.p->'draft'->>'body',
         CASE WHEN p.p->'draft'->>'status' = 'approved' AND p.p->'draft'->>'approved_by' = 'auto'
              THEN 'approved' ELSE 'pending' END,
         CASE WHEN p.p->'draft'->>'status' = 'approved' AND p.p->'draft'->>'approved_by' = 'auto'
              THEN 'auto' END,
         nullif(p.p->'draft'->>'hold_reason', '')
    FROM p
   WHERE p.p->>'action' = 'draft-follow-up'
     AND p.p->'draft'->>'channel' = 'email'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM drafts d
                      WHERE d.lead_id = (p.p->>'lead_id')::bigint
                        AND regexp_replace(coalesce(d.variant, ''), '[/+].*$', '')
                            = regexp_replace(p.p->'draft'->>'variant', '[/+].*$', ''))
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM leads l WHERE l.id = (p.p->>'lead_id')::bigint AND l.status = 'sent')
  RETURNING id, variant, status, approved_by, hold_reason
),
lost AS (
  UPDATE leads l
     SET status = 'lost', updated_at = now()
    FROM p
   WHERE p.p->>'action' = 'mark-lost'
     AND l.id = (p.p->>'lead_id')::bigint
     AND l.status = 'sent'
  RETURNING l.id
)
SELECT (p.p->>'lead_id')::bigint   AS lead_id,
       p.p->>'action'              AS action,
       (SELECT id FROM ins)        AS draft_id,
       (SELECT variant FROM ins)   AS variant,
       (SELECT status FROM ins)    AS status,
       (SELECT approved_by FROM ins) AS approved_by,
       (SELECT hold_reason FROM ins) AS hold_reason,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM lost)::int AS marked_lost
  FROM p;

nodes.name: Write Follow-Up
nodes.notes: Into drafts as 'pending' with hold_reason -- the exceptions queue -- or approved by this workflow when the gate passed it (the table re-checks, migration 020). Or the lead marked lost.
